title: Proving Ground: deploy scratchpad and fast-fail checklist
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for a small, high-risk model flip experiment in the proving ground (internal staging that touches 1% production cohort). Not a final runbook; this is my working checklist and hypotheses.

Goals:
- Validate KV cache warmup behavior for v3.2-quantized on 32-token prompts.
- Confirm p95 tail does not regress more than +40ms vs baseline under steady-state traffic.
- Ensure no more than 0.5% user-facing errors in the exposed cohort.

Scope / Traffic shape:
- Cohort: 1% of signed-in web clients (cohort tag: PG-1pct).
- Ramp plan: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1.0% over 60m (15m steps: 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0).
- Time window: low-traffic slot (US-west 03:00-06:00 PT).
- Baseline model: v3.1-stable. Candidate: v3.2-quantized-fast.

Warmup / priming tasks (pre-traffic):
- Run 500 synthetic requests with typical prompt family A to populate KV cache across 3 backends. Use sequence lengths 16, 32, 64.
- Run small A/B smoke set (10 prompts) hitting hallucination-sensitive checks and exact-match evaluation. Capture outputs.

Fast-fail triggers (immediate rollback if any hit):
- Error rate (5xx or 4xx transformer errors) > 1% for 5 continuous minutes in cohort sample.
- p95 latency increase > +200ms vs baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows.
- Quality delta: eval harness scoring drop > 4% absolute on the prioritized prompt set.
- Token-level drift: average next-token perplexity increase > 15% (debug metric).

Soft-signal thresholds (attenuate traffic when hit; require manual review before next ramp):
- p95 tail +40–200ms sustained 10m -> pause ramp and hold for 30m.
- Cost burn 2x expected token spend in cohort over 30m -> throttle to 0.5% and alert billing on-call.

Observability & checks to run continuously:
- Dashboards: PG-quickview (p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, errors, tokens/sec, GPU util).
- Synthetic probing: every 60s 3 probes (short, medium, long) routed through the cohort path and logged.
- Telemetry queries to run: error-rate(cohort) / rolling(5m), latency_p95(cohort), eval-score-delta(last-1h vs baseline).
- Logging: enable full debug sampling 0.1% for first 30m, collect model logits for flagged failures.

Pinning and client behavior notes:
- Client pinset: use runtime flag client.pin_model_version = v3.1 for baseline cohorts; PG-1pct will get v3.2 via routing policy only, no client change.
- If rollback triggered, route cohort back to v3.1 and remove v3.2 from routing table. Persist incident note in the rollback ticket with exact time window.

Rollforward criteria (need both):
- 2h stable window at 1% with no fast-fail triggers and p95 within +40ms.
- Quality checks: automated eval stable (<=2% delta) and manual spot-check of 50 random examples with no new hallucination class.

Post-deploy artifacts to collect:
- Example failures bucket (S3 path: s3://pg-artifacts/maya/v3.2/); include prompt, model output, traces, and model logits when available.
- Performance dump: p95 by minute, GPU temp, memory pressure logs, and model kernel selection trace for the warmup period.

Communication and playbook steps:
- Pre-rollout Slack ping: #deployments + @oncall. Include link to quickview and the smoke results.
- On any fast-fail: open incident in JIRA with template: [PG-ROLLBACK] timestamp, cohort, trigger metric snapshot, first-3 anomalous logs, immediate mitigations.
- Postmortem: short 48h writeup with hypothesis, telemetry, runbook gaps, and next steps.

Misc operational notes / hypotheses to validate:
- Hypothesis A: KV cache priming with 500 synthetic requests reduces cold p95 by ~20%. Test by comparing pre-warm vs no-warm data at 0.1% stage.
- Hypothesis B: Quantized kernel selection might pick slower fallback kernels for some sequence lengths; capture kernel traces to correlate.
- Hypothesis C: Small cohorts exhibit noisy evaluation; require at least 2h at 1% to really decide on quality regressions.

TODO / follow-ups (my notes):
- [ ] Add quick script to auto-create the PG cohort routing rule and tag requests for easy filtering.
- [ ] Bake in an automated throttle that reduces cohort to 0.2% on cost-exceeding rule (cost rule currently manual).
- [ ] Ask infra to expose kernel-selection logs to the quickview for the proving ground experiments.

Quick rollback command (ops cheat):
- curl -X POST $ROUTER/admin/reroute -d '{"cohort":"PG-1pct","target":"v3.1-stable"}'  (need to parameterize for safety; copy to ops slack on go-time)

Note to self: keep this doc light and pragmatic. Capture actual run timestamps and quick notes here during the rollout so I don't lose context.

End of scratchpad.
